headline: 11 Jamaat MPs challenge district-wise duties for ministers in High Court
summary: Lawmakers argue the government's decision to assign ministers and whips to oversee specific districts is unlawful and unconstitutional.
details: Eleven Jamaat-e-Islami lawmakers have filed a writ petition with the High Court challenging the legality of the government’s decision to assign ministers, state ministers, and whips responsibilities for specific districts.
The petitioners seek a declaration that the decision is unlawful and beyond the government’s legal authority, arguing it conflicts with the Rules of Business and the Constitution.

Senior Advocate Mohammad Shishir Manir, counsel for the petitioners, stated that a similar district-wise allocation of responsibilities was made in 2001 and was subsequently declared unconstitutional by the High Court.
The government's notification issued by the Cabinet Division on August 27 assigned 30 ruling party MPs, including ministers and state ministers, responsibility for 64 districts.
These assigned MPs are tasked with overseeing and coordinating law and order, anti-corruption, anti-drug efforts, good governance, transparency, and public welfare activities across the country.
caption:
Can ministers be assigned to oversee specific districts? 11 Jamaat MPs are taking the legal battle to the High Court.

Eleven Jamaat-e-Islami lawmakers have filed a writ petition with the High Court challenging the legality of the government’s decision to assign ministers, state ministers, and whips responsibilities for specific districts.

The petitioners seek a declaration that the decision is unlawful and beyond the government’s legal authority, arguing it conflicts with the Rules of Business and the Constitution.

Senior Advocate Mohammad Shishir Manir, counsel for the petitioners, stated that a similar district-wise allocation of responsibilities was made in 2001 and was subsequently declared unconstitutional by the High Court.

The government's notification issued by the Cabinet Division on August 27 assigned 30 ruling party MPs, including ministers and state ministers, responsibility for 64 districts.

These assigned MPs are tasked with overseeing and coordinating law and order, anti-corruption, anti-drug efforts, good governance, transparency, and public welfare activities across the country.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo

headline: Two arrested over headteacher’s death in mugging near parliament
summary: Ronjila Parvin, a primary school headteacher from Bogura, died after falling from a rickshaw when muggers pulled her bag in front of Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban.
details: Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) has arrested two people, including the prime suspect, in connection with the death of a primary school headteacher who fell from a rickshaw during a mugging incident.
The victim, Ronjila Parvin, was the headteacher of Bagbari Girls’ Government Primary School in Bogura. She had traveled to Dhaka from Bogura with her husband to consult an eye specialist.
The incident occurred around 6:30 am yesterday morning near the South Plaza area of the parliament complex. Two muggers on a motorcycle approached from behind and pulled at her bag.
During the struggle, Ronjila fell from the rickshaw, suffering severe head injuries and a fractured spine. She was rushed to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where she was declared dead.
The victim's husband, Abdul Matin, witnessed the entire incident. He later filed a murder case with the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station against two unidentified muggers.
The arrestees have been identified as Poni alias Para Poni and an associate. Rab-2 will hold a press briefing regarding the arrest of the suspects.
caption:
A primary school headteacher died after falling from a rickshaw when muggers pulled her bag in front of the parliament building.

Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) has arrested two people, including the prime suspect, in connection with the death of a primary school headteacher who fell from a rickshaw during a mugging incident.

The victim, Ronjila Parvin, was the headteacher of Bagbari Girls’ Government Primary School in Bogura. She had traveled to Dhaka from Bogura with her husband to consult an eye specialist.

The incident occurred around 6:30 am yesterday morning near the South Plaza area of the parliament complex. Two muggers on a motorcycle approached from behind and pulled at her bag.

During the struggle, Ronjila fell from the rickshaw, suffering severe head injuries and a fractured spine. She was rushed to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where she was declared dead.

The victim's husband, Abdul Matin, witnessed the entire incident. He later filed a murder case with the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station against two unidentified muggers.

The arrestees have been identified as Poni alias Para Poni and an associate. Rab-2 will hold a press briefing regarding the arrest of the suspects.
